purpose: Cancel expired pending-payment orders and release their native reservation items exactly once.
success_outcome: A deterministic 72-hour expiry run cancels only eligible orders, releases holds, and safely completes after retries or partial cleanup.
anti_goals: No YooKassa webhook or payment retry behavior.
No reservation finalization on payment success.
No custom queue, scheduler service, inventory ledger, or Medusa Core change.

forbidden_scope: FT-009 payment-provider calls, webhook, or credentials
production data, secrets, direct browser database access

success_checks: Hourly job selects only expired logical pending_payment orders with native pending status.
Native cancellation is followed by reservation deletion by line item.
Paid, canceled, non-pending, and unexpired orders remain unchanged.
Partial cleanup and repeated runs are idempotent and recoverable.
UTC 72-hour arithmetic is deterministic and tested.
T3 markers and semantic-pass evidence are recorded.
evidence_required: Expired, paid, canceled, and partial-cleanup integration fixtures.
Before/after reservation counts and sanitized retry evidence.
Typecheck/build/lint and full T3 protocol/recovery evidence.

stop_conditions: The job cannot distinguish eligible pending_payment state.
Cleanup is not retryable after a partial failure.
Installed Medusa cancellation/reservation APIs contradict the linked specs.
Verification cannot prove paid-order state is unchanged.
